source_title: Genie Francis Thanks Family for Supporting Her 50-Year TV Career in Daytime Emmys Speech - People.com
source_excerpt:
The ‘General Hospital’ star thanked her family while reflecting on her soap career while accepting the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards
Genie Francis received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Daytime Emmys on Friday, Oct. 30
Her husband, actor Jonathan Frakes, presented the honor with an emotional speech celebrating her career, their children and her impact on fellow actors
The General Hospital actress fought back tears as she accepted the award, noting that she is recovering from a broken ankle
Genie Francis received one of the biggest honors of her career with her family by her side.
The General Hospital actress, 64, who first portrayed the iconic Laura Spencer on the ABC soap five decades ago, accepted the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Daytime Emmys on Friday, Oct. 30. Her husband, actor Jonathan Frakes , presented the honor to her, delivering an emotional tribute.
“A lot of actors over the years have told me that Genie makes their work better,” Frakes, 74, said, referencing her collaborations with Patrick Swayze on North and South and Maurice Benard on General Hospital . He also recalled the lasting impact of her iconic General Hospital romance with Anthony Geary’ s Luke Spencer. “Without Genie, there is no Luke and Laura. And Tony Geary, he knew it,” Frakes said.
He remembered how Geary, who died last year at the age of 78, once dedicated part of an Emmy victory to Francis after her emotional departure from the soap. “He held the statue right up, and he said, ‘Genie Francis, half of this belongs to you,’” Frakes recalled. “He knew it. We all know it.”
Frakes, who has worked with Francis on 12 projects, also praised her professionalism and generosity toward her costars. “There is no one more prepared, collaborative, or helpful, or professional, or funny,” he said.
He then turned his attention to their family, saying Francis’ greatest lifetime achievement was their two children, Jameson and Eliza, who were in attendance.
The couple met while working on the short-lived primetime soap Bare Essence in 1982 and married on May 28, 1988. They welcomed Jameson in 1994 and Eliza in 1997.
By the time Frakes presented the award to his wife, Francis was already in tears. “It is with enormous pride and endless love that I present this Lifetime Achievement Award to my wonderful wife,” he said.
Francis, who said she is recovering from a broken ankle, received help from her children as she made her way onto the stage. “I am absolutely overwhelmed,” she began. “I want to thank my children for flying out here and for getting me up these steps. I’m getting over a broken ankle.” She added, “So thank you for supporting me — literally and figuratively.”
The actress also thanked those responsible for the tribute video, admitting it had already brought her to tears before she reached the stage. “I know 50 years sounds like an awfully long time, but it doesn’t feel like it to me,” Francis said.
“As they say, if you love what you do, you never work a day in your life,” she continued, before joking, “I wouldn’t go quite that far because doing party scenes in high heels is definitely hard work.”
“But honestly, I have had the most amazing ride, and I am so grateful,” she said.
Francis reflected on the many performers she has worked alongside throughout her career, naming Geary, Tristan Rogers , Susan Lucci , David Canary , Peter Bergman , Eric Braeden and Erika Slezak , as well as Benard and Michael E. Knight .
“I have had nothing but blessings, and a lot of fun, and the time has flown by,” she said. “I love what I do as much now as when I first started. The joy of doing the work, the day to day, has never left me.”
She concluded her speech by thanking her children for supporting her career and her husband for his continued devotion. “As always, I thank my husband for his unwavering support and love,” she said. “Truly, my cup runneth over.”
After accepting her award, Francis embraced her husband and shared a sweet kiss with him before the couple walked offstage together.
ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty
The recognition comes just months before Francis marks 50 years since her debut on General Hospital . She first stepped onto the set in February 1977 at just 14 years old.
“I want to offer my deepest gratitude to the leadership of NATAS for honoring me with this year’s Lifetime Achievement Award,” Francis said ahead of the ceremony. “This February marks 50 years since I first portrayed Laura on General Hospital . Stepping onto that set at just 14, I could never have imagined the extraordinary journey that lay ahead.”
Over the decades, Francis helped bring one of daytime television’s most memorable love stories to life as Laura, whose romance with Luke became a defining part of the show’s history. The characters’ 1981 wedding drew an estimated 30 million viewers, making it the most-watched daytime television event in history.
Francis’ portrayal of Laura has remained central to her career, with the actress continuing to appear on General Hospital through the years. The soap opera, which premiered in 1963, remains a staple of ABC’s daytime lineup.

In a statement announcing the honor, NATAS President and CEO Adam Sharp praised Francis’ lasting impact on the genre.
“We are thrilled to celebrate Genie Francis’ remarkable career. From Port Charles and beyond, she has left an indelible mark on the landscape of daytime television, and she continues to tackle bold topics as a courageous storyteller to this day,” Sharp said.
While General Hospital has been a defining part of her career, Francis has also appeared on several other daytime dramas, including All My Children as Ceara Connor, Days of Our Lives as Diana Colville and The Young and the Restless as Genevieve Atkinson.
Her credits extend beyond soaps too. Francis has appeared in series including Murder, She Wrote , Roseanne , Roswell and 3rd Rock from the Sun , as well as several Hallmark Channel films. She has also performed onstage in productions including Crimes of the Heart and See How They Run .
For Francis, however, her connection with General Hospital and the viewers who have followed Laura’s story for decades remains a particularly meaningful part of her legacy.
“I am deeply grateful to have been welcomed onto your television screens and into your homes for five decades; for the love, support and loyalty I’ve been given; and for the privilege of being a small part of your lives,” she said in her statement.
“Thank you to NATAS, my colleagues, the daytime community and, most of all, the viewers,” she continued. “My career in daytime television has truly been the adventure of a lifetime, and I am deeply honored by this recognition.”
